I played for just over an hour and tried 4 runs. In 2 of those runs, enemies stopped spawning. The first time, they disappeared for about five minutes, causing me to miss out on XP. In games like this, missing five minutes of XP is a death sentence. The second time, enemies stopped spawning indefinitely around the 18-minute mark, which is how I ended up winning a run on my fourth attempt. This bug really soured my opinion of the game so I just stopped playing. It's a shame because the game is quite fun, but I don't think I'll be playing it again any time soon. I should probably note that I was playing on the Steam Deck, so I'm unsure whether this problem is exclusive to the Deck.

Can't recommend it on it's current state. I remember having fun with the demo on a next fest a few months back. Didn't run into any major issues back then. They rushed this into 1.0 but it wasn't ready and it's not ready now either. Went back to the game after some time to find all my unlocks gone and a bug I hadn't seen before which makes enemies stop spawning for minutes at a time. This ruins the experience and your runs. Once the game is actually finished I would recommend it to people who are big fans of VS style games. I haven't seen it bring anything new to the genre thus far but it's a fun one. Devs took the early access tag out before it was fully cooked this is main reason I'm leaving a negative review. Will visit later on after some updates to update this if they finish it properly.

I wanted to revisit this review now that I've completed 100% of the game. All levels, all achievements, all challenges (most of which are not achievements for some reason), every shop upgrade, etc. The entirety of the original review is left at the bottom, which I left about 3 hours in. I still cannot recommend Nerd Survivors. It feels incomplete. There's a mechanic in the game, that I actually really like, called the Forge. You're given the ability to freely modify 24 types of weapons within a certain budget and choose three of them to take into levels. Some of these weapons are the best in the game. It was while developing my weapon of choice, the "Magical ♥♥♥♥♥♥' Bullets", I realized the amount of weapons available to modify and pick in the Forge outnumber the weapons that are always available, 24 to 14. This got weirder when I realized that there's 28 characters, and there's significant overlap between their starting weapons. Only two weapons are unique among the starting weapons and several weapons are the starting weapon for three characters. That information is included at the end of the review for your convenience. But this raises questions: Why does Pirate not start with a cannon? Why do the Lich and Cleric have the same holy magic when they included a Scythe? Why does the Ninja start with rotating shields when there's a Shuriken? These weapons are all available, in game, right now, in the Forge. I'm not sure there's a charitable read on this. It feels like they included the weapons, couldn't figure out how to balance them, and decided to let the players handle it. Speaking of balance, we gotta talk about leveling up. Even in Single Player games there are some options so powerful that they warp the game around themselves, and for the rest of this paragraph, that's Luchador. Luchador is a level-up option that gives an average of 70% crit damage muliplier every level. Combined with the Assassin Class, which gives 35% crit over 10 levels, this equates to a 500% generic damage multiplier over 20 levels. The next best you can get is double damage over 10 levels, specific to either physical or magic damage, from the Warrior or Wizard, respectively. This means there's really One Correct Build in the game, and that's to take Assassin and Luchador and 4 filler slots, preferably Cooldown Reduction and either Warrior or Wizard for two of them. Some characters (the best ones, as it turns out!) even have additional crit multiplier built into them, letting you reach 2000% critical damage multiplier or higher. Anything beyond 360% is already superfluous for most of the stage, as basic enemies will explode when crit *at all*, but this is how you take down stage bosses with little to no danger to yourself. And that's a great segue into talking about Fartomancy, which I will be referring to as "The Fart" from now on. The Fart is probably the strongest weapon in the game, leaving a cloud of noxious gas behind your character that ticks multiple times per second for Big Damage. Most bosses can't handle being farted on, becoming stunlocked from the constant damage before rapidly disintegrating. Extra projectiles only increase potency and even the hardest stage bosses can be killed in just a few seconds with some properly built farting. With extra projectile duration, which The Fart itself will happily provide at weapon level 3, you can shroud yourself in a protective layer of gas that enemies will simply run into and die. The Fart is also emblematic of the type of humor in the game, and I wish the developers were confident enough in their own sense of humor to not rely on memes and references. The first enemies in the game you see are Goblins trying to disguise themselves as seagulls, quickly joined by their friends, Goblins disguising themselves as other beach-related fauna. I honestly find that pretty charming! There's a green meatboy-shaped character with a prominent li'l booty named "Gray" that the character description insists is gray. These are good little jokes! They're much funnier than inexplicable Men at Work and Michael Jackson references, at least. But, they're also never expanded on. The closest thing to a continuation of the Goblin Cosplay Joke is being able to use a Goblin disguised as a Nerd as one of the characters. The meatboys, as far as I can tell, *only* show up as characters. Maybe they're expanded on in other games this dev did, but I didn't play those, and frankly I do not intend to. And all that ties up neatly into why the game feels incomplete to me. The weapons, the balance, the characters; everything is just a little... off. So I can't reasonably recommend Nerd Survivors unless you're really hurting for new Survivors-like content. --- The complete list of starting weapons and their associated character(s): Arcane Beam: (2) Wizard, Green Baraonda: (2) Underwear, Fighter BOOM-erang: (2) Nigel, Legend Cutting Edges: (3) Hot Line, Esme, Gray Fartomancy: (2) Pirate, Nerd Friendship: (1) Guard Invoke Destiny: (2) Lich, Cleric Knowledge: (2) Francis, Red Magic Missiles: (3) Violet, Cosy, Oracle Pizza!: (2) Mike, Chef Raudi: (1) Snob Sanctuary: (2) Ninja, Rose Shock Value: (2) Johnny, Greenish Star Magic: (2) Master, Thorn --- The original, annoyed review, for reference: The game is pretty aggressive about leaving a review after every level. So here's Mine: It's fine, but I would skip it unless you want to study the genre or have a compulsion or something. You could certainly do worse for $5 but when the game that inspired it is also $5 and strictly better, and there are tons similar and better games for that price point on Steam, it's hard to recommend Nerd Survivors over any of them. Hell, HoloCure is *free*. The big issue is that level-ups are bland. You take a "class" which gives a small passive bonus, except for critical hit damage which is a huge outlier for some reason. Upgrades like 3% crit, 0.1% HP regen; those are your level-up choices. Except, and I really can't get over how weird this is, critical hit damage, which starts at 60%. The 6th level tends to give a large benefit, like an additional projectile, but there's no hint as to what you'll get until you get to that level. The only way to get a new weapon, or to increase the potency of a weapon you already have, is to find treasure chests on the map. It's a good way to get the player to move around but it makes it so chests aren't fun bonuses like they are in similar games. It's heavily incentive, if not outright required, that you get them as soon as you can to the detriment of experience and levels. That's not a trade-off though: leveling up sucks! The first character you can get has the worst weapon you'll see for the first two hours or so. It's the only one I've found so far that both has to be aimed and that the aim of it matters. Most of the other weapons I've found, like the Pizza, automatically target a nearby enemy. The spinner, for whatever reason, always throws in front of you, in the way you were last moving. It's a weird choice when no other characters first weapon acts like that. The game tries to be funny but mostly does this through the medium of stale memes and ♥♥♥♥-size jokes. There's straight up a "size wink wink" joke in the shop, and one of the characters requires doing "69" of something. "It's a trap!" would normally come off as innocuous but in this game I *have* to be suspicious. So in conclusion, I can't recommend unless you're really into "Survivors" type games. Now quit asking me to leave a review every 10 to 20 heccin' minutes.
